title: What they said at the time

clips.q: I overreacted. I stopped all expansion, and once you stop, you know how hard it is to get the monster going again.
clips.who: **Howard B. Johnson**, to Forbes, 1978, as quoted in the International Directory of Company Histories[^1]

clips.q: My father felt that I should start at the top and work my way down.
clips.who: **Howard B. Johnson**, on becoming president at 26, as quoted in the same history[^1]

clips.q: Howard Johnson’s ice cream comes in 28 flavors and its food in one.
clips.who: A gag of the 1970s, as recorded in the International Directory of Company Histories[^1]

clips.q: We were more anxious to get rid of them than they were to get them.
clips.who: **Melvin Taub**, executive vice president of Prime Motor Inns, on the franchised restaurants, Orlando Sentinel, April 1987[^4]

clips.q: Howard Johnson was allowed to become tired and stale.
clips.who: **George Carter**, chairman of Franchise Associates, Orlando Sentinel, April 1987[^4]

clips.q: It’s definitely twilight time for Howard Johnson’s.
clips.who: **Walter Mann**, who ran a fan website about the chain, to the Associated Press, May 2005[^6]

clips.q: It’s not worth it to keep it open. We tried for four years.
clips.who: **Sally Patel**, co-owner of the Bangor restaurant, to the Associated Press, August 2016[^12]
